text: Generic plan and write kernel of the layer writer scripts. What: the writer scripts of the Components and Contours folders share one model. A script planner turns one layer into Change rows. A row can hold one edit. A collect function of the script family ( component_writer , outline_writer ) runs the planner on the chosen layers and fills a Plan . The script's Editor writes the edits, and apply_work makes that write ONE history.commit with operation="geometry" . How: apply_work calls editor.prepare for every layer BEFORE history opens, so native objects exist before the first init . Inside history, editor.write changes each layer and settle lets FontLab rebuild the layer caches. editor.retain names the native objects that the write removes; history.commit puts them first in the notification with deep history (FontLab issue 7641). An editor that removes nothing gives the two-argument notification. editor.check reads the font back: a value that FontLab did not keep raises RuntimeError . A failure after history started raises history.PartialWriteError ("... use Edit > Undo"). Why: the component and outline families used private copies of the same kernel. One App module keeps the Undo protocol, the read-back and the error texts the same everywhere. The two families keep their own collect and refusal policy: component_writer refuses the whole batch, and outline_writer lists and skips each refused glyph. This module imports only the standard library and stdlib-only App modules ( history ) at load time, so FontLab's 5-second cold import stays fast. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo. How to use (a family module):: from fontlabapp.masters.layers.writer import Change, Editor, Plan, apply_work class Shift(Editor): def write(self, layer, steps): ... apply_work(plan.work, "Shift", facts, Shift())

text: apply_work ( work : Work , title : str , facts : AutoFacts , edit : Editor , * , allow_bases : bool = False ) -> dict [ str , Any ] Write all edits as ONE native Undo step through history.commit. edit.prepare builds every native object BEFORE history opens. edit.write changes one layer; the write strategy decides what is kept. edit.retain names the native objects that the write removes (for a removed component: the component, its data and its builder); history.commit puts them first in the notification with deep history (fl#7641). An editor that removes nothing returns no objects, and the notification is the two-argument one. edit.check reads the font back and returns one text per edit that FontLab did not keep. Auto layers are never in work ; facts is a fresh history.scan_auto_facts. allow_bases passes the user's consent to edit bases of automatic composites to history.commit. No rollback is attempted: a failure after history started raises history.PartialWriteError ("... use Edit > Undo").
title: fontlabapp.masters.layers.writer.apply_work

text: Write font master vertical metrics as ONE native Undo step. What: write_master_metrics(package, {master: {field: value}}, title) writes ascender, descender, x-height, caps height and line gap of one or more masters through font_history.commit_masters (route A of issue 122 M2, measured for ascender and xHeight on FontLab 9.0.9790). The same flPackage.*_value setters are what Font Info uses ( fontinfo_data.cpp:577-581 ). Fields ( FIELDS ): ascender , descender , xHeight , capsHeight and lineGap . capHeight is an alias of capsHeight ( ALIASES ): the host registers flPackage.capHeight on the same setter ( pyflpackage.cpp:1405-1414,3545 ); results use capsHeight . lineGap is the master line gap of Font Info ( flPackage.lineGap_value ). The separate hhea line gap is in master otherData ; no measured setter exists for it, so a name such as hhea_line_gap is refused as unknown. Refusals ( ValueError ) come before any history call: an empty request, an unknown field, a value that is not a finite real number, and every refusal of commit_masters (GUI thread, Font window, unknown master). Read-back: FontLab stores these values as C++ double ( flpackage.h:603-654 ). A stored value reads back as the same double, so the tolerance ( TOLERANCE ) only absorbs a last-bit difference; a rounded or clamped value fails the read-back, all values are restored and font_history.RolledBackError is raised. Known host defect (fl#8574): after Undo/Redo, the font-metric guidelines show 3 of 9 until updateFontMetrics() or a reopen (see font_history ). scripting.write_font_info stays unchanged. Offline tests prove the call order only.
title: fontlabapp.metrics.master_writer

text: Shared plan, write and panel parts of the Metrics scripts (advance edits). What: the Metrics scripts (Round Advances, Scale Advances, Tabular Width, Centre In Advance, Italic Sidebearings, Zero-Width Marks) share one model. A planner turns one layer into a LayerPlan (outline shift dx and new advance width ) or a skip text. survey plans every target layer, commit writes all pending plans as ONE Undo step and reads them back, and the non-modal MetricsPanel (from panel_type() ) shows a live preview. How: commit uses fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit with the "geometry" policy. Auto layers are listed and never edited. A glyph that owns an auto layer is listed and skipped as a whole. Layers with a metrics link or expression are listed and skipped. A base of auto composites is refused until the user ticks ALLOW_AUTO_LABEL for exactly the glyphs that change now. shift_and_set moves the outline in place ( applyTransform ), never through a clone, because flShape.clone() drops raw node flags and notes (FontLab issues 8516 and 8538). Why: each script then holds only its constants, its planner and a small build() . This module imports only the standard library at load time. PythonQt and FontLab load inside the functions; panel_type() loads the Qt panel class. Offline tests do not prove native Undo/Redo/reopen. How to use (a script):: from fly.ap.metrics.panel.model import LayerPlan, make_plan, panel_type class RoundAdvances(panel_type()): TITLE, KEY, HEADERS, ACCENT = "Round Advances", "metrics_round", ("Width",), (1,) def build(self): ... def subtitle_hint(self): return "Rounds advances." def planner(self, package, glyphs): return lambda layer, master: make_plan(...)

The write goes through fontlabapp.core.history.glyphs.commit with operation="geometry" : refusals first, then init history, shift_and_set per layer, stamp, one notify of the layers and their glyphs, stamp, read-back. Return {"layers", "glyphs", "auto_skipped", "mismatches"} . Nothing to change returns zeros and makes no history call. A refusal raises ValueError ; a failure after history started raises history.PartialWriteError .

text: survey ( glyphs : list [ Any ], masters : list [ str ], planner : Planner , * , facts : AutoFacts | None = None ) -> list [ Entry ] Plan every glyph/master layer. Skipped layers are listed with a note. Skip, in this order: a missing layer ( MISSING_NOTE ); an auto layer ( AUTO_LAYER_NOTE ); any other layer of a glyph that owns an auto layer ( AUTO_GLYPH_NOTE ; the geometry policy refuses such glyphs); a layer with a metrics link ( LINK_NOTE ); a layer the planner skips (its text). A manual composite is also skipped when its base moves in this plan. Pass the existing whole-font component facts to follow unselected intermediate glyphs. Without facts, only selected layers supply edges.

text: Non-modal panel: masters, script controls, live preview table, Apply, Close. What: a subclass sets TITLE , KEY , HEADERS (preview columns after "Glyph · master") and ACCENT (column numbers shown bold in the link colour), and fills in build , subtitle_hint and planner . Optional hooks: target_glyphs , empty_message , sync_controls . How: every control change recomputes the preview from the live font. Component facts are shared by transitive skips and rebuild warnings; construction, Use selection and Apply refresh them. Apply plans again with fresh facts and writes through metrics_panel.commit (one Undo step, geometry policy). The panel binds to the font that was current when it opened; a switched font is refused. A base of auto composites needs the ALLOW_AUTO_LABEL tick, and the tick belongs to exactly the glyphs that change now. Why: the preview can never be stale at Apply, and slot errors stay in the status line instead of reaching FontLab. Show it with scripting.show_script_dialog(Subclass, Subclass.KEY) .

text: The native Alignment Zones backend: capture, check, bounds and apply. What: backend() returns the zone_editor.Backend for the current font. It reads and writes PostScript zones the way Font Info does ( fontinfo_data.cpp:565-620 ): per master setMaster(name, False) , read ps_zonesT / ps_zonesB , write convertZonesToGuidelines(top, bottom) then updateZonesFromGuidelines() . Apply stages every changed master through font_history.commit_masters (ONE Undo step, issue 122 M2 route A, measured on FontLab 9.0.9790). Values: zones are plain zone_data values. Both native lists hold positive widths (FontLab stores a bottom zone as a guide with a negative extension, flpackage.cpp:12433-12523 ). Origins carry no native id: a zone key is "Top:<name>" or "Bottom:<name>" from capture. FontLab keeps zone names unique per list, so apply finds the source zone of a retained row by its baseline kind and name, and copies that native zone ( flZone(zone) ): its tags and lock state stay. A new row gets a new flZone . What the route changes: convertZonesToGuidelines replaces every zone guide of a written master. The guides get new ids, x-centre 0 and the custom font-guideline style; only position, width, name, tags and lock are kept. Font Info does the same. Refusals before any history call: RowRefusal (a ValueError ; the dialog stays usable) for an empty zone name (FontLab would rename it T: 500 ; Editor.add names new rows as FontLab does), a duplicate name in one list (FontLab would add .1 ) and a zero-width row whose kind FontLab reads differently ( zone_native_rules.is_top ); then the GUI-thread and Font-window guards; then ValueError(STALE_TEXT) for a stale snapshot. Rollback: a failure before the notification restores the zones with the same convert/update calls, so FontLab re-creates the zone guides with new ids; the RolledBackError text says so ( RESTORED_TEXT ). Non-zone guides are not rebuilt ( flpackage.cpp:12456-12462 ). Restoring the original guide objects would need guidelinesHost , which is unmeasured. fl#8554: this route never calls flModelProducer.getClipboardData , so the serializer arity defect does not affect it. The serializer modules ( zone_capture , zone_prepare , zone_write_plan ) stay held. Known host defect (fl#8574): after Undo/Redo, the font-metric guidelines show 3 of 9 until updateFontMetrics() or a reopen (see font_history ). Offline tests prove the call order only.

text: apply ( before : Snapshot , changes : tuple [ Change , ... ]) -> Snapshot Write every changed master as ONE Undo step; return the new baseline. Refuse rows first ( RowRefusal ), then off the GUI thread or without an active Font window ( font_history.require_font_window ), before any master switch. Check that the font still equals before and that every row can be stored as planned, then font_history.commit_masters . Print the queued glyph ids note to Output ( edit_guards.disclose ). Then read back every master and the current master again ( capture ); a difference or a failed read raises history.unstored_error , whose rule this module keeps: the text makes no claim about Undo. Return before with each changed master's zones replaced by its verified plan. No ValueError is raised after commit_masters returns, so a caller may treat a ValueError as a refusal made before any write.
title: fontlabapp.metrics.zones.native.apply

text: open_layer_rows ( rows : tuple [ tuple [ RowItem , ... ], ... ], * , expected_id : int , master : str , deadline : float | None = None ) -> None Open exact glyph/layer occurrences in rows, in ONE verified fresh native tab. What: each row is a tuple of items. An item is (glyph name, exact layer name) , or SPACE ( (None, "") ) for one space. Rows are separated by one line break; an empty row keeps its line, as in open_named_tab . Use it for stacked or side-by-side layer comparisons (Master Text Comparison). How: the complete immutable request is validated first. Then every requested layer must exist in the font expected_id ( flPackage.id , the current font). Only then are native symbols built: a layer item is an fgSymbol with its own layerName ; a space is the text symbol list fgSymbolList(" ") and a line break fgSymbolList("\n") , the same text form that open_named_tab uses for line breaks. The tab opens through the shared fresh-tab fence ( _open_symbols ). master fences the current source master; it does not overwrite the layer of an item. Why: scripts must not build fgSymbol lists or call requestContent themselves. Any failure before the tab opens opens no tab. Native qualification (space text symbol, layer per symbol) remains open.
title: fontlabapp.proof.tabs.named.open_layer_rows

text: Menu actions and tool windows that are safe to remove under signal dispatch. What it does: OwnedMenus adds QActions to FontLab menus (or to one menu it owns) and shows widgets in tool windows. Each item gets an integer token. remove(token) and close() undo the items in a safe way. Why: A menu callback or a window button often removes its own item. If the host disconnects or deletes the QAction or QWidget while its signal still dispatches, PythonQt deletes the signal receiver twice and FontLab crashes (AGENTS.md: disconnect before deleteLater ; never tear down in a slot). Every slot that this class connects counts a dispatch depth. While the depth is above zero, remove and close queue their work. One shared zero-delay DeferredBatch timer runs the queue after the outermost slot returns. Each queued item runs once. How to use: menus = OwnedMenus(qt, fontlab, error_sink=sink) token = menus.add_action("Edit", "My action", callback) menus.remove(token) or menus.close() at unload. token, window = menus.tool_window(widget, "Title", on_close=done) . Rules: GUI thread only. qt is the PythonQt module and fontlab is the FontLab module; the caller passes both in. Callbacks take no arguments. Their errors go to error_sink(error, owner) and never reach Qt. QAction.text is a property in PythonQt, not a method. Guard scope: The dispatch guard covers only the slots that this class connects: menu triggered and the tool-window close. A signal that the caller connects itself (for example a button in the tool window) does not raise the depth. If such a slot calls remove or close , the teardown runs at once, inside that dispatch. Such a slot must queue its own call, for example with QTimer.singleShot(0, ...) . Subclasses wrap their own slots with _slot (Glyport's plugin host does this for Apply/Cancel). Cold import: stdlib plus fontlabapp.core.signals.deferred and fontlabapp.qt.safe .

text: Keep PythonQt widget pointers alive during native list conversion. What it does: qt_list converts a native QList of object pointers with cyclic GC off. main_window finds FontLab's main window with the same safety. Why: PythonQt wraps each pointer as a Python object. That allocation can start the cyclic collector, which can free a Python-owned widget that is still in the list. The next pointer then dangles and FontLab segfaults in PythonQtPrivate::wrapPtr (measured on FontLab 9.0.9780). Thread rule: GUI thread only, and the guard enforces it. gc.disable() is process wide. A call from another thread could re-enable collection while the GUI thread is still converting. The guard does not stop an explicit gc.collect() or reference-count destruction. Missing window: main_window raises MainWindowNotFound when FontLab has no main window. It is a RuntimeError with the old text, so older callers that catch RuntimeError or match "main window not found" keep working. New callers catch the class: the off-thread refusal stays a plain RuntimeError and is therefore never taken for a missing host. Cold import: stdlib only. Callers pass fontlab and qt in.
title: fontlabapp.qt.safe

text: Paint over FontLab's glyph editor: one overlay per visible glyph window. What it does: EditorPainters lets a script register painter callbacks. FontLab calls each callback once per laid-out glyph, after the native glyph layer is painted. Each call gets a PaintContext with the glyph-to-canvas map, the canvas-to-view map and a ready QPainter . How to use: painters = EditorPainters(qt, fontlab, error_sink=sink) where qt is the PythonQt module and fontlab is the FontLab module. token = painters.register("after_native_layer", callback) starts the work. painters.remove(token) stops one painter. painters.close() stops all of them. After the last painter is gone, the poll timer stops and every overlay is detached. layer_filter is "active" (default), "inactive" or "all" . document_id limits a painter to one font ( package.id ). Inside the callback, draw with context.painter and map glyph units to pixels with context.glyph_to_canvas then context.canvas_to_view . Native facts (FontLab 9.0.9780, measured by Glyport; evidence glyport-ui/probe-editor-paint.json ): - The native canvas paints the viewport from an event filter and fills it opaquely. A Python pre-paint leaves no visible pixel. Only painting after the native layer works, so before_native_layer raises ValueError here. - A transparent child widget of the viewport paints after the native canvas. This module uses one such child per viewport. - A glyph unit maps to a pixel as the native glyph paint does: glyph transform, then text-block transform, to canvas units, then flCanvas.mapToViewportF to pixels. Kerning is already in the glyph transform. Why this design: - New glyph windows appear at any time. A 250 ms poll finds them. Hidden (closed) tabs stay alive, so only visible windows get an overlay. - Callback errors go to error_sink . Nothing raises out of paintEvent : an exception there, with a QPainter active, crashes FontLab (AGENTS.md landmines). - The painter is saved and restored around every callback. One plugin cannot leak pen, brush or transform state into the next. - Teardown disconnects each signal before deleteLater . A widget deleted with live Python slot targets crashes FontLab (double delete in PythonQtSignalReceiver ). - Maths come from fontlabapp.contours.affine . Native widget lists come through fontlabapp.qt.safe.qt_list (GC off during conversion). Compare fontlabapp.qt.painting.drawing.Drawing : that class paints one given widget. This module is a registry over all glyph windows. Glyport's fontlab_glyport.drawing.editor subclasses it. The subclass adds the Glyphs UnsupportedCapability refusal for the before-native phase and the layer_resolver wiring.

Constructor keywords that name no parameter set a Qt property or connect a signal after construction, as PySide2 does. Anything ambiguous or unmapped keeps the native call, and its native error. text: same ( left : Any , right : Any ) -> bool Equality that never lets PythonQt compare a native slot with another type. PythonQt's slot comparison casts both operands to slot objects; comparing a native slot with a bound method of the same object segfaults FontLab (pqs-g04/fixtures/crash2-disconnect.md).
title: pythonqtside._app_cleanup.same

text: slot_forwarder ( slot : Any ) -> Callable Connect a native slot through a Python function. PythonQt passes every signal argument to a native slot, so clicked.connect(label.clear) fails with "wrong number of arguments"; Qt drops trailing arguments the slot does not take. The forwarder retries with fewer leading arguments and remembers the count that worked. Holding only Python functions in PythonQt's handler list also keeps its disconnect comparison away from native slots.
